article_title: Promoting preservice teachers’ multiperspective professional vision in virtual learning environments – On the effects of modeling videos and prompts during video-based lesson analysis
citation: Janeczko, J. M., Lehmkuhl, A., Junker, R., Zucker, V., Meschede, N., & Holodynski, M. (2026). Promoting preservice teachers' multiperspective professional vision in virtual learning environments – On the effects of modeling videos and prompts during video-based lesson analysis. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-025-10546-2
title: Teacher education programs should use video-based virtual learning environments for individualized promotion of professional vision
description: The article recommends that teacher education programs adopt video-based virtual learning environments that provide individualized learning paths, immediate feedback, and adaptive progression to promote professional vision. The VLE enables learners to progress at their own pace, with each learning unit requiring a defined level of competence before advancing. The study showed that such environments improved multiperspective professional vision compared to untreated controls.
requirements: The VLE must provide preprogrammed feedback based on expert assessments and adaptive learning paths based on preservice teachers' learning progress.
constraints: The content of the VLE must be adapted to the subject and school type, including knowledge input, classroom video selection, analysis tasks, master ratings, and feedback.
target_learners: preservice teachers in elementary science education
target_learning_goals: multiperspective professional vision of classroom management and instructional support
examples: The study's VLE consisted of five modules with increasing complexity, combining knowledge input via animated videos and quizzes with video analyses using closed and open response formats with automated feedback.
key_sources: Janeczko, J. M., Lehmkuhl, A., Junker, R., Zucker, V., Meschede, N., & Holodynski, M. (2026). Promoting preservice teachers' multiperspective professional vision in virtual learning environments – On the effects of modeling videos and prompts during video-based lesson analysis. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-025-10546-2

article_title: Metacognition design framework to aid metacognitive skill development in university students supported by the virtual learning environment
citation: O'Neill, E. J., Fulton, C., Matthews, J., & Hensey, C. (2026). Metacognition design framework to aid metacognitive skill development in university students supported by the virtual learning environment. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-025-10574-y
title: Use the VLE to extend metacognitive influence on student activity outside class time with realistic staff input, and re-frame educators as designers
description: The article recommends harnessing VLEs as more than repositories: "Virtual Learning Environments provide a unique, and potentially powerful, opportunity to influence student learning outside standard class time with realistic levels of staff input". The Metacognition Design Framework operationalizes this by mapping learning journeys and aligning technology via affordance analysis, providing "a practical way to re-frame educators as designers, increasing educator design capacity". Design sequences give educators a graphical, adaptable planning tool linking face-to-face and online components.
requirements: Educators create module-specific Metacognition Design Sequences from the generic blueprint
Affordance analysis aligning each learning task's requirements with technology or face-to-face options
constraints: Technology is 'the tool' and not 'the solution'; social and human dimensions of the context must also change
target_learners: university students in blended or fully online modules
examples: Guidance notes in online Appendix 1 explain planning a Learning Journey and applying the I-SEE strategies; Appendix 2 aligns technology with the strategies through affordances
key_sources: O'Neill, E. J., Fulton, C., Matthews, J., & Hensey, C. (2026). Metacognition design framework to aid metacognitive skill development in university students supported by the virtual learning environment. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-025-10574-y

article_title: The Effectiveness of a Programme-Based Vocabulary Learning Strategies for Developing English Vocabulary for EFL Female Students at Taif University
citation: Ismaiel, N. M., & Al Asmari, A. A. (2017). The Effectiveness of a programme-based Vocabulary Learning Strategies for Developing English Vocabulary for EFL Female Students at Taif University. Advances in Language and Literary Studies, 8(3), 113-125. https://doi.org/10.7575/aiac.alls.v.8n.3p.113
title: Vocabulary Learning Strategies Training Programme
description: A 12-week vocabulary learning strategies training programme for EFL students, based on Schmitt's (1997) VLS taxonomy, covering determination, social, memory, cognitive, and metacognitive strategies. The programme was delivered to the experimental group alongside their regular English course.
requirements: Delivered alongside a regular EFL course over 12 weeks
constraints: Studied only with Saudi female EFL students at Taif University
key_sources: Ismaiel, N. M., & Al Asmari, A. A. (2017). The Effectiveness of a programme-based Vocabulary Learning Strategies for Developing English Vocabulary for EFL Female Students at Taif University. Advances in Language and Literary Studies, 8(3), 113-125. https://doi.org/10.7575/aiac.alls.v.8n.3p.113

article_title: Evaluating a preclinical orthodontic training using haptic-enhanced VR simulation system: a longitudinal study.
citation: Liu Luwei, Qin Jinwei, Pan Yongchu, Wang Hua, Lu Xiaoqing, Chu Fengqing, Wang Lin, Hao Aimin, Yan Bin, Yuan Siyang. (2025). Evaluating a preclinical orthodontic training using haptic-enhanced VR simulation system: a longitudinal study. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-07036-7
title: Virtual orthodontic training system combining the VLNP online platform and the VSTES haptic VR simulator
description: A two-part virtual training system developed by Nanjing Medical University for preclinical orthodontic bracket bonding. The online Virtual Learning Network Platform (VLNP) lets students "undertake unlimited practice of all the procedures on the virtual learning environment in their own time", while the offline Virtual Simulation Training and Evaluation System (VSTES) provides haptic force feedback via two force-feedback devices and a 3D mouse, simulating the full bracket-bonding process with automated scoring and real-time feedback. Software copyrights are registered (online 2024SR0073414, offline 2021SR1708239).
requirements: Requires force-feedback hardware and a 3D mouse for the offline haptic section; online training requires only a computer mouse.
constraints: The article states the online VLNP supports only a two-dimensional environment inconsistent with the real clinical setting, and the offline system's micro-displacement accuracy and movement rate need improvement.
target_learning_goals: psychomotor skills of orthodontic bracket bonding, including cleaning, etching, rinsing, drying, and three-dimensional bracket positioning
examples: 26 postgraduates completed one week of online VLNP training and six weekly offline VSTES sessions, assessed by 3D laser scanning of bracket positions before and after training.
key_sources: Liu Luwei, Qin Jinwei, Pan Yongchu, Wang Hua, Lu Xiaoqing, Chu Fengqing, Wang Lin, Hao Aimin, Yan Bin, Yuan Siyang. (2025). Evaluating a preclinical orthodontic training using haptic-enhanced VR simulation system: a longitudinal study. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-07036-7
